complexity.notes: The header comment is honest about the key point: at these toy parameters (D = 16, L = 4) the Theorem 5 oracle spends more leaf products per wanted entry than a direct inner product, and the subquadratic bound needs N >= D^18 = 2^72, so in pure Python this runs as an enormous-constant O(n^2) — asymptotically identical to the previous two-pointer submission and orders of magnitude slower in wall clock. The added prime-selection sweep alone costs Theta(d^2 / log d) for d distinct values, and the straightforward oracle path makes the per-convolution-instance work Theta(d^2) anyway, so the machinery buys nothing at any reachable scale. The O(n^4) worst case is hash-adversary-driven: the output itself can be Theta(n^2) triples, and the found/rejected set lookups degrade against adversarially colliding integer keys. Impressively documented and structured for what it is, but the deleted 20-line sort-and-sweep does the same job at every n a judge will ever see.
complexity.summary: Reduces 3SUM to Convolution-3SUM by hashing the distinct values into buckets modulo a collision-minimizing prime, then to Exact Triangle via hashing modulo small primes (2 and 3), with the resulting sparse-triangle queries answered by a toy-parameter port of the Alman–Vassilevska Williams thin-product oracle when there are at most 200 distinct values and by a brute-force common-neighbour test above that. Candidates are filtered by exact integer witness checks, elements in overfull buckets are handled by direct scan, and multiplicities are verified against value counts before output.
